limitations_and_boundaries: The study does not rule out the possibility that axonal material may also be engulfed.
The precise function of microglia at synaptic sites and the long-term consequences of disrupting microglia function on synaptic circuits remain a mystery.
The selected source chunks do not report a rescue, reconstitution, reversal, or epistasis experiment; that rung of the causal evidence chain remains untested within this extraction scope.

incorrect_items.description: The claim states 'CR3/C3-dependent phagocytic signaling is a key molecular mechanism underlying microglial engulfment of developing synapses.' The source chunk (0b295ba6e5568eeaa990) says 'we hypothesized that C3 ligand-receptor signaling may be one molecular mechanism' — this is a hypothesis, not a confirmed claim. The extraction presents it as a positive claim without indicating it is a hypothesis, which overstates the evidence.

The claim 'Engulfment of RGC inputs by microglia is regulated by neuronal activity.' is supported by the source chunk (01d5b02edc8b5e8e2a23) which states 'determine that this process is regulated by neuronal activity.' However, the task 'su_d50f0304e535da77598c3b28:1' is described as 'Assessment of engulfment under altered neural activity conditions (details not provided in chunks).' This task is not present in the source chunks; the actual experiments are described in chunks 4 and 5 (TTX and forskolin injections). The task item is incorrect because it claims details are not provided, but they are.

missed_core_items.description: The extraction omits the key result that microglia engulfment is developmentally regulated, with high engulfment at P5 and significantly reduced at P9.
missed_core_items.source_excerpt: During a developmental period of robust pruning (P5), engulfment was high (Figures 2B and 2Di). As few as 4 days later (P9), when much of the pruning is nearly complete, engulfment of RGC inputs was significantly reduced (Figures 2B and Dii).

missed_core_items.description: The extraction omits the key result that microglia preferentially engulf inputs from the less active (TTX-treated) eye and fewer from the more active (forskolin-treated) eye, demonstrating activity-dependent engulfment.
missed_core_items.source_excerpt: When mice were injected with TTX and vehicle in the left and right eyes, respectively, microglia phagocytosed significantly more inputs from the less active TTX-treated eye (CTB-594, red) as compared to the vehicle-treated eye (CTB-647, blue) (Figures 3B and 3C). Likewise, mice injected with forskolin and vehicle engulfed significantly more inputs from the vehicle-treated eye (CTB-647, blue) as compared to the more active forskolin-treated eye (CTB-594, red) (Figures 3E and 3F).

missed_core_items.description: The extraction omits the key result that CR3 KO mice have sustained deficits in eye-specific segregation at P10 and P30, with increased overlap of ipsilateral and contralateral projections.
missed_core_items.source_excerpt: Consistent with the hypothesis that microglia mediate complement-dependent synaptic pruning, a statistically significant increase in ipsilateral and contralateral input overlap was observed in P10 and P30 CR3 KOs as compared to WT littermate controls (Figures 7A–7C).

missed_core_items.description: The extraction omits the key result that minocycline treatment (pharmacological inhibition of microglia) reduces engulfment and causes deficits in eye-specific segregation.
missed_core_items.source_excerpt: Similar to CR3 KO data, minocycline (P4–P8; 75 mg/kg) treatment during the peak of the pruning period resulted in reduced microglial phagocytic function (i.e., reduced RGC input engulfment) at P5 and a statistically significant deficit in eye-specific segregation at P10 (Figures S6C–S6E).

missed_core_items.description: The extraction omits the key result that C3 KO mice have an identical 1.3-fold increase in VGlut2-containing synapses as CR3 KOs.
missed_core_items.source_excerpt: Consistent with our previously published work (Stevens et al., 2007), adult C3 KO mice had an identical 1.3-fold increase in VGlut2-containing synapses as compared to WT littermate controls (Figure S7).
